evidence: The survivor explicitly uses "# 1. bipartition by BFS colouring" and maintains "0 = left, 1 = right"; the defeated solutions likewise build global "groups" from a bipartite coloring.
affordance_in_statement: It is guaranteed that the microservices can be split into two groups such that every conflict pair connects one group to the other; no conflicts within a group.
removal_suggestion: Remove the bipartiteness guarantee and state that the conflict pairs form an arbitrary simple undirected graph. The solver would then need to find an independent set of size k rather than obtain one directly from bipartition sides.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: BFS-color each connected component, choose the larger color side in each component, and truncate the resulting independent set to k vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: It is guaranteed that the microservices can be split into two groups such that every conflict pair connects one group to the other; no conflicts within a group.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It appears to aggregate color classes globally and select from one global side, rather than choosing the larger side independently for every connected component. A component can have its larger side assigned either color, so the global color class need not contain a maximum independent set.
It appears to use the same global bipartition-side selection strategy, which can fail on disconnected graphs because each component may need a different side orientation.
It appears to construct global groups from BFS coloring and choose between those groups, instead of combining the larger color class from each connected component.

recommended_edit: Replace the bipartite-graph guarantee with a statement that the conflict graph is arbitrary, while keeping the input and output formats unchanged.
regression_risk: This may restore the already-defeated models if their coloring code does not validate bipartiteness and happens to produce a valid independent set on the hidden arbitrary graphs.
